summary.headline: Krystal Q2 FY27 revenue rose 46.25% YoY to Rs 414.47 crore, but EBITDA margin eased to 6.0% from 6.32% on higher employee cost.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 reached Rs 414.47 crore, up 46.25% YoY and 14.9% QoQ, with H1 revenue at Rs 775.18 crore (up 27.82%). EBITDA excluding other income grew 38.82% to Rs 24.86 crore, but margin moderated to 6.0% from 6.32% as employee cost rose to 75.9% of revenue from 72.3%. PAT grew 41.66% to Rs 18.67 crore in Q2, helped by a lower effective tax rate of 12.5%. Management highlighted the Citelum India acquisition, new segments (solid waste management, solar EPC, technical FM) and a Rs 2,980-3,000 crore order book spanning about 3 to 3.5 years.

financial_highlights.change: +38.82% YoY; margin vs 6.32% in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Employee cost as % of revenue (Q2 FY27)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 63.84 crore (borrowings Rs 144.64 crore, cash Rs 80.80 crore)

segments.name: Manpower and related services
segments.commentary: Contributed about 91% of H1 FY27 revenue; the core business, with government about 65% and corporate about 35% of revenue and receivables.

segments.name: Catering and related services
segments.commentary: Contributed about 9% of H1 FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Citelum India (city lighting, acquired 100%)
segments.commentary: Acquisition completed; management targets Rs 300-350 crore annual revenue over 3-4 years with about Rs 100 crore planned investment. Bidding has started; asset-light, project-driven model.

segments.name: Solid waste management (new segment)
segments.commentary: Current processing capacity about 400 TPD (incl. TMC Vasai-Virar); target 800-1,000 TPD via active bidding.

segments.name: Solar EPC and technical FM (new)
segments.commentary: First solar EPC order from DMER, a 15-year contract on premises where Krystal already provides facility management. Technical FM introduced to target O&M and turbine maintenance at electrical plants.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin band of 6.25% to 7.5%, which management aspires to stay within.
Management is confident of a good revenue number for FY27 (ending 31 March 2027); said about 46-47% of projected revenue is already achieved against a projected growth band of 18-23%.
Citelum target: Rs 300-350 crore annual revenue over 3-4 years.
Management expects new contract start-up dips in margin to stabilise over time as O&M and technical businesses scale.
Management is evaluating inorganic opportunities with startups and companies with national O&M reach, robotics and AI.
capex_capacity: Citelum: planned investment of about Rs 100 crore in engineering capabilities, technology platforms and business expansion over 3-4 years.
Solid waste processing capacity about 400 TPD today, targeted to rise to 800-1,000 TPD.
Network of 33 branches (36 offices cited), 5 warehouses; 49,971 on-site employees; 540+ customers across 4,700+ locations as of 30 Sep 2026.
Citelum team retained; management says no lead time needed to mobilise projects given existing captive team, processes and pre-qualification.
demand_pricing: Order book of about Rs 2,980-3,000 crore, to be executed over the next 3-3.5 years; government about 65%, corporate about 35%. Segment-wise breakup not disclosed.
Tenders evaluated worth over Rs 12,000 crore; bids submitted worth about Rs 4,200-4,500 crore in H1 FY27.
Historical conversion of newer tenders stated at 8-10%, explicitly not a committed number.
H1 FY27 added 59 new corporate customers (31 in Q2); FY26 added 177 corporate customers.

Major wins include Rs 26 crore SE Central Railway Bilaspur (24 months), Rs 134 crore MSRTC Mumbai and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (3 years), Rs 296 crore LC Infra-Krystal Consortium share (40%) for Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0 in Pune and Nagpur, Rs 33 crore and Rs 6.6 crore Maha Mumbai Metro, Rs 27.6 crore AP BC Welfare hostels sanitation, Rs 17 crore Maharashtra Rajya Sahakari Sangh (5 years), Rs 8.75 crore Kosol Energie manpower at Bavla, Gujarat.
Margin dip attributed to start-up working capital and other costs on newly won larger contracts; management says newer technical and O&M contracts are less manpower-intensive and margin-accretive.
Management is working with customers to pass through the cost impact of statutory employee costs under the four labour codes effective 21 November 2025; some customers already paying.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from 6.32% to 6% despite strong revenue growth, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new large contracts require upfront working capital and startup costs, causing a temporary dip; margins are expected to stabilise as contracts mature and O&M/technical businesses grow. No quantified timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline for the Rs 3,100 crore order book and expected revenue in next 6-12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is about Rs 2,980-3,000 crore, to be executed over 3-3.5 years. About 46-47% of projected FY27 revenue is achieved; management is confident of a good FY27 revenue number.

qa_highlights.question: Will Citelum focus on government or private projects, and does it need heavy assets to reach Rs 300-350 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Both government and private. Business is project-driven (design, installation, commissioning, O&M) and asset-light, with existing pre-qualification and team; more detail promised in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the historical tender conversion rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conversion of newer tenders has historically been 8-10%, not a committed figure, and depends on tender structure and criteria.

qa_highlights.question: What is the government vs corporate split of revenue and receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: About 65% government and 35% corporate for both revenue and outstanding receivables; mix was 70:30 earlier and management sees a 60-70% government range going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How will bidding discipline protect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: A bid committee evaluates each tender on projected P&L, operational capability, working capital and profitability before bidding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pursuing acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; evaluating startups and companies with national O&M reach, robotics manufacturing engagement and AI-related businesses.

risks_watch: Employee cost at 75.9% of revenue (vs 72.3%); recovery of statutory cost increases from the four labour codes from customers is still in progress.
Receivable days at about 118; working capital intensity on new contracts may keep pressure on cash and margins.
Tender conversion of 8-10% on about Rs 4,200-4,500 crore of bids; order book depends on converting pipeline.
Citelum revenue target of Rs 300-350 crore in 3-4 years depends on winning tenders; management gave limited detail on current order inflow.
Concentration on government clients (about 65% of revenue and receivables).
Net debt of Rs 63.84 crore and expansion plans (about Rs 100 crore for Citelum) to be funded.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book and new verticals, but defensive when asked about margin compression, which management attributed to contract start-up phases. Several answers on specifics (order-book breakup, customer billing, Citelum progress) were deferred or unquantified.
key_quotes: As in now that we add our O&M businesses, our technical businesses etc., you will see that the margin deficiency is then taken good care of by these businesses.
We are not going to need any lead time when we acquire a project.
So, we are a company with a national footprint.

adds.what: Solid waste management processing capacity to 800-1,000 TPD from about 400 TPD today (target via active bidding)
Citelum India city lighting vertical (acquired 100%), asset-light, Rs 300-350 cr annual revenue target over 3-4 years

growth.why: Management says about 46-47% of projected FY27 revenue is already achieved against a projected 18-23% growth band (midpoint ~20.5%), backed by a Rs 2,980-3,000 crore order book over 3-3.5 years and new Citelum and SWM verticals, though segment-wise order breakup and new-capacity timing are not disclosed.
